उ: u, Vedic encl. copula. 	—1. and; also; further;  used in one (oftenest the latter) of two clauses or sentences containing things alike or slightly contrasted (e. g. 7814, 799), esp. in anaphora (e. g. 795, 909); 	—2. now, straightway,  w. verbs present and past and w. imperatives or imperative subjunctives, 7110, 8515, 855, 878; often followed by sú, right soon; --pragṛhya [see 1122a2, 138c] when combined with átha (9016), úpa (7814), mā́ (878); for 839 and 8411, see notes; 	—3. in classical Skt. only w. (atha, kim, and) na, and not, 2114, 2717.
उक्थ: ukthá, n. utterance, esp. of devotion; praise; hymn of praise; invocation. [√vac, 1163a.]
उक्थवर्धन: uktha-várdhana, a. strengthening, i. e. refreshing or delighting one's self with hymns of praise. [acct, 1271.]
उक्ष्: √ukṣ [252] or vakṣ (ukṣáti, -te; aúkṣīt; ukṣiṣyáti; ukṣitá; -úkṣya). sprinkle; besprinkle; drop, intrans., 757. [secondary form (108g end) of √*uj or ug: cf. ὑγ-ρός, ‘wet’; Lat. ūvens (*ugvens) caelum, ‘the dropping sky’; w. ukṣán, ‘besprinkler, impregnator, bull,’ cf. Goth. auhsa, ‘bull,’ Eng. ox, and for mg, √vṛṣ.] + pra, sprinkle before one by way of consecration.
उग्र: ugrá, a. mighty; exceedingly strong; terrible.  [√vaj, 252, 1188; see ójas.]
उग्रशासन: ugrá-śāsana, a. having a terrible way of ruling; as m. a strict ruler. [1298a.]
उच्: √uc (úcyati [only w. preps]; uvóca [783b], ūcivā́ṃs [803]; ucitá). be pleased; be wonted; ucitá: 	—1. with which one is pleased; proper; suitable; 	—2. accustomed.
उच्च: uccá, a. lofty; uccaís, adv. [1112c], high; of sound, loud. [fr. uccā́, adv. instr. (1112e) of údañc.]
उच्चय: uccaya, m. heap, pile, collection. [√1ci + ud, ‘heap up.’]
उच्चावच: uccāvacá, a. high and low; various; diverse. [ud + ca w. ava + ca, 1314b.]
उच्छिष्ट: úcchiṣṭa, ppl. left; as n. leavings, esp. of a sacrifice or of food. [√śiṣ + ud.]
उज्जयिनी: ujjayinī, f. Oujein, name of a city, Ptolemy's Ὀζήνη. [fem. of ujjayin, ‘victorious, ’ √ji + ud, 11833: of like mg are Νικό-πολις and Cairo.]
उञ्छ्: √uñch (úñchati, uñcháti; úñchitum). sweep together, glean. [for *unsk, *vansk, orig. ‘wipe, or whisk, i. e. sweep’: cf. AS. wascan, ‘wash,’ Eng. wash and whisk.] + pra, wash away; wipe out, 232.
उत: utá, conj. and; also; even; connecting words, clauses, and sentences; repeated: uta…uta…(uta), both…and…(and); at beg. of verse, 7812; --uta vā: or even, 8720; or, 8414 (cf. atha, 6); apy uta, also.
उत्तम: uttamá, a. 	—1. up-most; highest; best, esp. at end of cpds; excellent; chief; 	—2. (out-most, i. e.) ut-most; extreme; last (see 676N.), 9920. [úd, ‘up, out,’ 473.]
उत्तमगन्धाढ्य: uttamagandhāḍhya, a. rich in excellent odors, 1519. [uttama-gandha + āḍhya.]
उत्तमाधममध्यम: uttamādhamamadhyama, a. highest and lowest and midmost; best and worst and middling. [uttama + adhama + madhyama, 1257.]
उत्तर: úttara [5252], a. upper; higher; 	—1. being above, (opp. adhara) 7018; having the upper hand, victorious, 8121; 	—2. northern (on account of the Himālayas, cf. udañc); ā_uttarasmāt, as far as the north (side), 10510; 	—3. the left (because in prayer the face is turned eastward: cf. dakṣiṇa), 9922; 	—4. (like ὕστερος) the latter (opp. pūrva); later; following, 9922; -am, as adv. finally, last, 10412; 	—5. as neuter subst. the final element of a phrase of salutation, 603; 	—6. answer, retort. [úd, 473: cf. ὕστερος, ‘latter’; Eng. comp. ut-ter, ‘outer.’]
उत्तरतस्: uttaratás, adv. northward; to the north of; w. gen. [1130], 10513. [uttara.]
उत्तरपुरस्तात्: uttara-purastāt, adv. north-east of; w. gen., 1130.
उत्तरलोमन्: úttara-loman, a. having the hair above, with the hairy side up.
उत्तरापथ: uttarā-patha, n. the northerly way; the north country.
उत्तरेण: úttareṇa, adv. northerly; north of, w. acc. [1129], 1025. [uttara, 1112c.]
उत्तरोत्तर: uttarottara, 	—1. a. higher and higher [1260]; -am, as adv. more and more, 243; 	—2. as n. answer to an answer [1264]; wordy talk, 249. [uttara + uttara.]
उत्पल: utpala, n. a Nymphaca, i. e. water-lily or lotus. [√paṭ + ud.]
उत्सव: utsavá, m. 	—1. an undertaking, beginning; 	—2. feast-day, festival, 254, 4916. [√2su + ud, ‘set a-going’; but the development of 2 from 1 is not clear.]
उद्: úd, prefix. never used alone; up, up forth, out. [cf. AS. ūt, Eng. out: see uttara, uttama.]

√ud or und (unátti; unná, uttá; -údya). 	—1. spring; boil or bubble up; flow; 	—2. wet, bathe. [cf. Lat. und-a, ‘wave’; w. ud-an, ‘water,’ cf. ὕδ-ωρ, Eng. wat-er; w. ud-ra, ‘otter,’ cf. ὕδ-ρα, ‘water-snake,’ Eng. otter.] + sam, flow together; wet.
उदकुम्भ: uda-kumbhá, m. water-jar; jar with water.
उदगयन: udag-ayaná, n. north-course (of the sun), or the half-year from the winter to the summer solstice. [udañe.]
उदग्दश: údagdaśa, a. having the seams upward. [udañc + daśā, ‘fringe, border, seam.’]
उदङ्मुख: udaṅ-mukha, a. having the face to the north. [udañc, 1249a, 161.]
उदञ्च्: údañc [409b], a. directed upward; directed northward (on account of the Himālayas), cf. uttara), northerly; in cpds, udak, 1249a. [ud + añc, 407.]
उदय: udayá, m. a going up; rising (of the sun). [√i (1148. 1a) + ud.]
उदर: udára, n. belly. [orig., perhaps, ‘rising, swelling,’ √ṛ + ud: for mg, cf. the relation of belly to AS. belgan, ‘swell.’]
उदार: udārá, a. (like Eng. exalted, i. e.) noble, excellent. [√ṛ + ud, ‘rise.’]
उद्बाहुक: údbāhuka, a. having the arms out or extended. [ud + bāhu, 1305, 1307.]
उद्य: udya, grdv. to be spoken or pronounced. [√vad, 1213c end, cf. 963c.]
उद्यम: udyama, m. raising (of the hands to work); exertion. [√yam + ud.]
उद्यान: udyā́na, n. 	—1. a walking out; 	—2. (place for walking out, i. e.) garden, park. [√yā + ud, 1150.]
उद्विग्नमनस्: udvigna-manas, a. having a terrified mind, distressed. [√vij.]
उन्मत्तदर्शन: unmatta-darśana, a. having a frantic look. [√mad + ud.]
उन्मार्ग: unmārga, m. by-way, evil way. [ud + mārga.]
उन्मार्गगामिन्: unmārga-gāmin, a. going in evil ways.
उप: úpa, 	—1. vbl prefix. to, unto, toward; opp. of ápa; 	—2. prep., w. acc., unto, 8115; w. loc., in, 775; 	—3. in noun cpds [1289b], denoting something near, accessory, or subordinate. [cf. ὑπο, Lat. s-ub, ‘under.’]
उपकनिष्ठिका: upakaniṣṭhikā (sc. aṅguli), a. f. next to the little, i. e. the third (finger). [upa (mg 3) + kaniṣṭhaka, 1222d.]
उपकर्तृ: upakartṛ, m. one who does kindness; benefactor. [√1kṛ + upa, q. v.]
उपकार: upakāra, m. friendly service; kindness. [√1kṛ + upa, q. v.]
उपकारिन्: upakārin, a. the same; as m. benefactor. [√1kṛ + upa, q. v.]
उपचार: upacārá, m. a coming to or waiting upon;  pregnantly, (polite) attention; (correct) procedure, i. e. duty. [√car + upa.]
उपत्य: upatya, a. lying under. [upa, 1245b: cf. ὕπ-τιο-ς, ‘lying under, supine.’]
उपत्यका: upatyakā, f. land lying at the foot (of a mountain). [upatya.]
उपदेश: upadeśa, m. a pointing out to, a direction;  instruction; advice. [√diś + upa.]
उपनायन: upanāyana, n. investiture. [technical term, see √nī + upa.]
उपपृच्: upapṛ́c, a. clinging close to, w. gen. [√pṛc  + upa.]
उपभृत्: upabhṛ́t, f. wooden cup (used in sacrifices),  see srúc. [‘tó-bringer,’ √bhṛ (383b) + upa.]
उपभोग: upabhoga, m. enjoyment; eating. [√2 bhuj + upa, q. v.]
उपमश्रवस्: upamá-śravas, a. having highest glory; as m. Upamaśravas, a name like Μεγιστο-κλῆς or Ὑψι-κλῆς.
उपमा: upamā́, f. comparison, image; and so likeness,  resemblance; at end of cpds, having likeness with…, like…. [√1mā + upa, ‘compare.’]
उपमार्थ: upamārtha, m. purpose of an image; -ena, figuratively. [artha.]
उपयोग: upayoga, m. ap-plication; use; utility. [√yuj + upa.]
उपरि: upári, adv. above; as prep., w. gen. [1130], above; at end of cpd [1314f], upon, 3916. [cf. ὑπείρ, *ὑπέρι, Lat. s-uper, ‘over.’]
उपला: úpalā, f. upper mill-stone; cf. dṛṣad.
उपवञ्चन: upavañcana, n. a tottering unto, a faltering approach. [√vañc + upa.]
उपवन: upavana, n. small forest, i. e. grove. [upa (mg 3) + vana.]
उपवीत: úpavīta, ppl. wound about, esp. with the sacred cord; as n. [1176a], the being surrounded with the sacred cord; the cord itself. [√vyā + upa, 954c.]
उपवेश: upaveśá, m. a sitting down. [√viś + upa.]
उपवेशि: úpaveśi, m. Upaveśi, name of a man.
उपसंग्रहण: upasaṃgrahaṇa, n. the clasping and taking to one's self (the feet of another), as sign of great respect. [√grah + upasam. ]
उपसेवा: upasevā, f. a serving; a being devoted to. [√sev + upa.]
उपाख्यान: upākhyāna, n. subordinate tale; episode, 11. [upa (mg 3) + ākhyāna.]
उपादान: upādāna, n. the taking to one's self; appropriation. [√1dā + upa_ā, ‘take.’]
उपानह्: upānáh, f. sandal; shoe. [‘under-bond,’ √nah + upa (247): for mg, cf. ὑπό-δημα, ‘sandal.’]
उपान्त: upāntá, n. proximity to the end; edge; immediate neighborhood. [upa (mg 3) + anta.]
उपाय: upāya, m. approach; that by which one reaches an aim; means; expedient, 392; stratagem; advantage, 396. [√i + upa, 1148. 1a: for mg, cf. Eng. to-ward, as an adj.]
उपोषित: upoṣita, ppl. having abstained (i. e. from food), having fasted; as n. [1176a], fasting.  [√3vas + upa, q. v.]
उभ्: √ubh (ubhnā́ti, umbháti [758]; ubdhá; -úbhya). unite; couple. [cf. ubhá.] + apa, bind, fetter.
उभ: ubhá, a. both. [cf. ἄμφω, Lat. ambō, AS. nom. fem. neut. bā, Goth. nom. neut. ba, nom. masc. bai, w. dental extension, bajoϸs, all meaning ‘both,’ Eng. bo-th: orig., perhaps,  ‘couple,’ and akin w. √ubh.]
उभय: ubháya [5254], a. of both sorts; both. [ubhá.]
उभयतस्: ubhayátas, adv. from both sides; in both cases. [ubháya, acct !]
उभयतःसस्य: ubhayataḥ-sasya, n. having a crop at both times, i. e. bearing two crops a year.
उरग: urá-ga, m. serpent. [‘breast-going,’ ura for uras: for mg, cf. khaga.]
उरस्: úras, n. breast. [perhaps, ‘a cover,’ from √1vṛ, ‘cover,’ 1151. 1b, w. a specialization like that in Eng. chest, ‘thorax.’]
उरु: urú, f. urvī́, a. (prop. encompassing, and so, like Eng. capacious) extensive, wide, great; as n. (like Ger. das Weite) the distance.  [√1vṛ, ‘encompass,’ 1178a: cf. εὐρύ-ς, ‘wide.’]
उरुव्यचस्: uru-vyácas, a. having wide embrace, wide extending. [acct, 1298b.]
उरुष्य: √uruṣya (uruṣyáti). to distance, i. e. escape; put another in the distance, i. e. save. [urú, ‘the distance,’ 10612.]
उरूणस: urū-ṇasá, a. having broad snouts. [urú (247) + nás, 193, 1315c: acct, 1298b.]
उल्ब: úlba and úlva, n. enveloping membrance of an embryo. [for *ur-vá, √1 vṛ, ‘enclose, ’ 1190. cf. Lat. rol-ra, ‘covering, womb.’]
उल्बण: ulbaṇá, a. lumpy, knotty, thick, massy. [ulba, for *urva, hence ṇ, 189.]
उष्: √uṣ (óṣati; uvóṣa; aúṣīt; uṣṭá). burn. [for cognates, see the collateral form √1vas, ‘light up,’ also uṣás, usrá, etc.: cf. εὕω, ‘singe’; αὔω, ‘kindle’; Lat. ūr-o, ‘burn,’ and ustus = uṣṭá-s; AS. ys-le, ‘glowing ashes.’]
उषस्: uṣás [415b], f. morning-red; dawn; personified, Dawn. [√1vas, ‘light up, dawn,’ 252: cf. ἠώς, Aeolic αὔως, Lat. aurōra, *ausōs-a, ‘dawn’; radically cognate also is Eng. eas-t, ‘the point where day breaks’: see uṣ and usra.]
उस्र: usrá, a. bright; of or pertaining to the dawn; as f., usrā́, dawn. [√1vas, ‘light up,’ 252, 1188, 181a: w. us-rā́, cf. Old Germanic Aus-t-rō, a goddess of the (year-dawn,  i. e.) spring-light, and AS. Eos-t-ra, the name of whose festival, easter, ‘Easterday, ’ occurring in April, was transferred to the Christian festival that replaced it; for t between s and r, see under svasṛ: see uṣ and uṣas.]
